newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-VALENCONY SAVES TWICE TO HAND NICE THIRD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VALENCONY SAVES TWICE TO HAND NICE THIRD CUP WIN.

text.p: Goalkeeper Bruno Valencony was Nice's hero with two penalty saves as they beat Guingamp 4-3 in a shootout to win the French Cup for the third time on Saturday.
The last ever final at the Parc des Princes ended in a 1-1 draw after extra time.
Nice, relegated from the first division, will play in the European Cup Winners' Cup as a second division side next season.
"That's the magic of the cup," a beaming Nice coach Silvester Takac said afterwards.

"The French Cup is a beautiful competition that gives all the little sides a chance," he added, naming third division Nimes who were losing finalists last year and went on to play in the Cup Winners' Cup.
Nice also won the cup in 1952 and 1954. They were losing finalists in 1978.

Valencony saved Guingamp's first penalty from Stephane Carnot, the substitute who had brought his side back into the match in the second half with his deft promptings from midfield and dangerous free kicks and corners.
After defender Luis Gomis shot Nice's fourth penalty over the bar, Valencony saved again from Claude Michel and Dutchman Arjan Vermeulen sealed victory by converting the last spot kick.
Earlier, Nice opened the scoring in their first deep incursion into Guingamp territory when, from a Roberto Onorati free kick on the right, they won a corner on the left in the 21st minute.
Defender Youssef Salimi rose to head home the corner taken by midfielder Thierry de Neef.

Guingamp, playing in their first final, equalised 13 minutes from time through defender Nicolas Laspalles, one of their best players, who broke past the defence to beat Valencony with a fierce shot after Nice failed to clear a free kick by Carnot.
Nice had the better of the first half once they had found the net, but Guingamp were more adventurous after the interval and had several chances to get back into the match before their equaliser.
Carnot, a bandy-legged dead ball specialist who was not in Guingamp's starting line-up because of a thigh problem, almost scored direct from a corner in the 69th minute.

Valencony managed to push the ball away on the goal line as the ball curled at the near post, just preventing Carnot from repeating his goal against Paris St Germain on the same ground in a league game earlier in the season.
Valencony kept Nice in the match in the dying minutes of normal time, saving from tall striker Charles-Edouard Coridon and Michel when the midfelder was clean through.
Coridon also failed to snach victory for Guingamp when he shot just over the bar from a good position eight minutes from the end of extra time.
Nice's Liberian substitute James Debbah could have scored in the dying minutes but he was foiled by a fine last-ditch tackle by Guingamp's Polish defender Marek Jozwiak.
"We were very strong mentally," Takac said. "I had a feeling victory would come, and when it went to penalties I was sure we would win.
"We have been working on our penalties two or three times a week since the cup started (for first divison sides in January)."
Teams:

Guingamp - 1-Angelo Hugues; 2-Jerome Foulon (15-Jean-Luc Vannuchi 97), 4-Marek Jozwiak, 5-Gheorghe Mihali, 3-Nicolas Laspalles; 7-Richard Lecomte (14-Stephane Carnot 50), 6-Claude Michel, 8-Yannick Baret, 11-Charles-Edouard Coridon; 10-Daniel Moreira (12-Christophe Horlaville 63), 9-Christopher Wreh.

Nice - 1-Bruno Valencony; 2-Henri Savini (14-Thierry Cretier 77), 4-Youssef Salimi, 5-Frereric Taratian, 6-Olivier Fugen (12-Arjan Vermeulen 91), 3-Louis Gomis; 7-Frederic Gioria, 8-Thierry de Neef, 11-Roberto Onorati; 9-Andrezj Kubica, 10-Mohamed Chaouch (15-James Debbah 83).
